title: Enabling Electrical Readout of Néel vector reversal in a van der Waals Antiferromagnet
authors: Raghvendra Posti, Ravi Kumar Bandepalli, Wenhao Liu, Anshuman Sahoo, Pratyush Saud, Zixin Zhai, Aswin L. N. Kondusamy, Zhenhong Cui, I-Hsuan Kao, Aalok Tiwari, Thomas Poirier, James H. Edgar, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Bing Lv, Jyoti Katoch, Simranjeet Singh
abstract: Owing to its robustness against external perturbations and intrinsically ultrafast dynamics, the Néel vector in antiferromagnets (AFMs) can enable the development of next-generation spintronic and magnonic devices for memory and computing applications. To realize AFM-based magnetic memory devices, one of the key requirements is to demonstrate electrical readout of 180-degree reversal of Néel vector in thin film AFMs, which remains critically missing. In this work, we report experimental demonstration of a novel transport methodology to detect Néel vector reversal in atomically thin films of a van der Waals (vdW) based A-type AFM. For this, we utilize spin-dependent electronic band properties of CrSBr by coupling it to a spin-polarized layer, separated by a tunnel barrier. In this configuration, the spin-dependent tunnelling magnetoresistance (MR) becomes sensitive to the relative orientation between the magnetization of the reference electrode and the interfacial sublattice magnetization of the AFM layer, in turn enabling electrical detection of the Néel vector orientation. Importantly, the observed MR can also reveal 180-degree reversal of Néel vector in even-layers of CrSBr, wherein adjacent sublattice magnetic layers are exactly compensated and the net magnetization vanishes and thus establishes a broadly applicable strategy for electrical detection of Néel vector in vdW-based AFMs.
summary: This work reports an experimental breakthrough demonstrating electrical readout of Néel vector reversal in vdW antiferromagnets using $	ext{CrSBr}$. By constructing a tunnel junction with a ferromagnetic electrode, the authors achieved a measurable magnetoresistance (MR) signal that flips polarity when the AFM's magnetic order is reversed. This establishes a robust and generalizable strategy for building next-generation spintronic memory devices based on AFMs.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is demonstrating an electrical readout mechanism for the $180^\circ$ reversal of the Néel vector ($\mathbf{N}$) in thin-film van der Waals antiferromagnets (AFMs). This capability is crucial for developing next-generation AFM-based spintronic and magnonic memory devices.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated this readout by utilizing a spin-dependent tunneling magnetoresistance (MR) measurement in $	ext{Co}/	ext{hBN}/	ext{CrSBr}$ heterostructures. They showed that reversing the Néel vector results in an opposite hysteresis pattern in the MR response, confirming electrical sensitivity to $\mathbf{N}$ orientation.
method: The methodology involves fabricating vertical tunnel junctions using mechanical exfoliation of vdW materials ($	ext{CrSBr}$, $	ext{hBN}$) and measuring the magnetoresistance (MR) as a function of applied magnetic field ($B$) and bias voltage ($V_{	ext{bias}}$).
model_or_system: The system is based on atomically thin, A-type vdW AFMs like $	ext{CrSBr}$, which possess sublattices ($\mathbf{m}_A$, $\mathbf{m}_B$) defining the Néel vector $\mathbf{\hat{N}}$. The measurement relies on the spin-dependent tunneling magnetoresistance (MR), modeled by the Jullière tunnelling model, between a ferromagnetic (FM) electrode ($	ext{Co}$) and the AFM layer.
key_observables: Magnetoresistance (MR) response exhibiting clear two-level (low/high resistance) switching behavior; the reversal of this MR hysteresis pattern when the initial magnetic field polarity is reversed.
important_parameters: The measurements are sensitive to bias voltage ($V_{	ext{bias}}$), temperature ($T$), and applied magnetic fields, with key transitions observed near $T_N \sim 130-140\ 	ext{K}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the measured MR is dominated by spin-dependent tunneling through the tunnel barrier, making it sensitive to the relative alignment between the FM magnetization and the AFM sublattice magnetization.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematics of the A-type AFM order and the proposed tunnel junction setup. Key results show field-dependent and bias-dependent MR hysteresis loops that reverse polarity when the initial magnetic field used for initialization is reversed, confirming $\mathbf{N}$ reversal.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the critical gap (electrical readout of Néel vector) to proposing a specific tunnel junction geometry. It then details experimental measurements showing spin-valve behavior and conclusively proves Néel vector reversal by observing opposite MR hysteresis patterns upon reversing the initial high magnetic field polarization.
why_interesting: While primarily condensed matter/spintronics, the concept of using quantum transport phenomena (spin-dependent tunneling) to read out a fundamental symmetry property ($\mathbf{N}$ reversal) is highly relevant to developing novel quantum memory elements and controlling spin states in solid-state systems.
